NATIONAl-FOREWORD This Indian Standard (First Revision) which is identical with IEC Pub QC 001002�3 (1998) 'IEC Quality assessment system for electronic components (IECO) - Rules of procedure - Part 3 : Approvalproecdures' issued by the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendation of Basic Standards on Electronics and Telecommunication Sectional Committee and approval of the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council. The revision has been undertaken in order to align Indian Standard with the latest International Standard as under IEC quality assessment system for electronic components (IECQC), it is obligatory for each member country to adopt IECQC standards as their national standards without any change . The text of the IEC standard has been approved as su itable for publication as Indian Standard with~ut deviations. Certain conventions are, however, not identical to those used in Indian Standards . Attention is particularly drawn to the following: Wherever the words 'International Standard' appear referring to this standard, they should be read as 'Indian Standard'. IEC QUALITY ASSESSMENT SYSTEM FOR ELECTRONIC COMPONENTS (IECQ) RULES OF PROCEDURE
PART 3 APPROVAL PROCEDURES

( First Revision)

o. An introduction to the types of approval available under the IECQ
0.1 Introduction
This clause describes briefly the types of approval available under the IECa as detailed in the requirements given in clause 2 and the following clauses. These approvals are summarized below with further information given in Figure 1 and Table 1.

0.2

Approval of manufacturers and other organizations

This level of approval is a prerequisite to seeking any other type of approval listed in clause 2 and the following clauses and is applicable to manufacturers, distributors, independent testing laboratories and specialist contractors wishing to become approved under the IECa. The requirements of this type of approval are described in clause 2, Requirements for the approval of an organization. It should be noted that, when carrying out the appraisal, the National Supervising Inspectorate (NSI) is required to take into account any relevant certificate to ISO 9001, ISO 9002 and ISO/IEC Guide 25 issued by an organization declared competent to do so by the appropriate national authority.

0.3 0.3.1

Approvals available to manufacturers Choice

A manufacturer has the approvals detailed in 0.3.2 to 0.3.4 available to him. A particular manufacturer's choice of approval will depend on existence of current approvals, product range, available applicable specifications, and expected manufacturing development.

0.3.2

Qualification Approval of electronic components

This type of approval is applicable to an identified electronic component or range of components for which detail specifications exist. Where a detail specification does not exist, it is permissible for a manufacturer to prepare a detail specification in accordance with ac 001002-2, clause 1, for publication within the System. aualification Approval (QA) is granted to a manufacturer when it has been established that the components meet the requirements of specifications which are approved for use within the IECa.

The requirements ,')f this type of approval are described in clause 3, Qualification Approval of
electronic components. A prerequisite for obtaining this type of approval is that a manufacturer must have, or obtain, manufacturer's approval to clause 2 (see 0.2 above). 5

IS QC 001002-3: 2000 IEC QC 001002�3 (1998)

0.3.3

Capability Approval of an electronic component manufacturing facility

This type of approval is applicable to an identified component manufacturing process for which an applicable IECO generic or sectional specification describing Capability Approval (CA) exists. It is granted to a manufacturer when it has been established that his capability for manufacturing processes and quality control methods (including design aspects if applicable) covering a specific component technology fulfils the requirements of the relevant generic specification. The requirements of this type of approval are described in clause 4, Capability Approval of an electronic component manufacturing activity. A prerequisite for obtaining this type of approval is that the manufacturer must have or obtain manufacturer's approval to clause 2 (see 0.2 above). NOTE A manufacturer may apply for approval in accordance with clause 2, at the same time as submitting his application for QA or CA under clauses 3 or 4.

0.3.4

Technology Approval for electronic component manufacturers

Technology Approval (lA) is a method of approval which has evolved to meet the needs of manufacturers and incorporates the most recent principles and techniques in the management of quality. It provides for the use of statistical methods and tools, continuous improvement and procedural fleXibility. This type of approval is applicable to an identified electronic component manufacturing activity for which a Technology Approval Schedule (lAS) exists. The requirements for this type of approval are described in clause 6, Technology Approval of electronic component manufacturers. A prerequisite for obtaining this type of approval is that a manufacturer must have or obtain manufacturer's approval to clause 2 (see 0.2 above). NOTE1 A manufacturer may apply for approval in accordance with clause 2, at the same time as submitting his application for TA under clause 6. TA will not be granted in advance of manufacturer's approval. NOTE2 A manufacturer approved to clause 2, wishing to obtain TA, should note th�at there is requirement to produce a Technology Approval Declaration Document (TADD) (see 6.4).

0.4

Approvals available to specialist contractors

This type of approval is applicable to any specialist contractor wishing to obtain Process Approval (PA) to carry out "contracted work" under the IEeO. This type of approval is applicable where a relevant Process Assessment Schedule (PAS) exists.

The reqUirements for this type of approval are described in clause 5, Approval of specialist contractors' processes and/or products within the electronic components industry.
A prerequisite for obtaining this type of approval is that the specialist contractor must have or obtain specialist contractor approval to clause 2 (see 0.2 above).

1. Approval of a National Supervising Inspectorate
1.1 Description and general requirements

1.1.1 A National Supervising Inspectorate (NSI) is the national organization responsible for the surveillance of all procedures for quality assessment necessary for the System. This includes the evaluation for the approval and surveillance of manufacturers, distributors, specialist contractors and independent testing laboratories, the supervision of the certification of conformity and the audit testing of approved components.
NOTE For the purpose of the (ECa , an audit test is a component test carried out on a random basis by the NSf, or under its.direction, to verify the proper application of the specification and the correctness of the test

results of the manufacturer. 1.1.2 a) b) An NSI shall be free from any influence which could prevent it from acting in an impartial manner, shall have a staff sufficient in number, technical competence and skill to carry out adequately its surveillance and supervisory responsibilities, should have for audit purposes those test facilities which ' are necessary for all normal measurements within its technological areas as defined in 1.2.2. Where some of these test facilities are not available in its own institution, the NSI shall have access to facilities in an approved independent testing laboratory which may be outside its own geographical area. In limited areas of high technology it is acceptable to use complex or specialized test equipment at an approved component manufacturer's factory. The components of one manufacturer shall not be tested in another component manufacturer's premises, except with the written agreement of the former. The result of all tests under such conditions shall be confidential to the NSI, and d) shall ensure that its representatives are under an obligation not to disclose any confidential information obtained in the course of their duties.

c)

1.1.3 In order to operate under the System, the NSI shall be approved by the Inspectorate Co001002-1, subclause 1.4.3). ordination Committee (ICC) (see

ac

1.1.4 The jurisdiction of an NSI covers all surveillance activities under the System within a defined geographical area, for which approval has been granted. 1.1.5 An NSI appointed by a National Authorized Institution (NAI) of a participating country can, after the approval by that NAI and by the ICC, delegate the authority for a defined technological area to another NSI. 1.1.6 When an NSI subcontracts any part of the inspection, it shall ensure that its responsibilities and obligations for the inspection conducted on its behalf are fully met. The NSI shall ensure and be able to demonstrate that its subcontractor is competent to perform the services in question and complies with the applicable criteria stipulated in the present clause 1 and with any additional requirements for the work being subcontracted. 1.1.7 The NSI snan record and retain details of its investigation of the competence and compliance of its subcontractors, and maintain a register of all subcontracting. These details shall be submitted to the ICC for approval in accordance with 1.7.1. 9

IS OC 001002-3: 2000 lEe OC 001002-3 ( 1"' )

1.1.1 Details ot the NSls and their subcontractors approved to operate under the System shall be Included in 001006. Register ot Participating Countries.

1.2.8

National documents

This section shall include or make reference to written working instructions which serve as guidance documents to the NSI, covering the items listed below: the approval of manufacturers; the approval of independent testing laboratories; the approval of distributors; approval of specialist contractors; surveillance inspection visits; the Qualification Approval of components; Capability Approval, Process Approval and Technology Approval; the application and control of the use of the Mark of Conformity and Certificate of Conformity ; calibration system requirements; audit testing of components by the NSI. This section shall also list any relevant documents providing additional information. All documents listed in 1.2.8 of the NSSA shall be made available to participating countries on request.

1.3

Examination of NSSAs

1.3.1 All members of the ICC shall consider each application for full membership (see 001002-1, subclause 1.4) and inform the Secretary within three months of the despatch of the application from the Secretariat

ac

whether they have any objections against the information presented; where applicable, whether they agree with the choice of a mentor NSI (see 1.5.2). The NSls of full members shall moreover inform the Secretariat whether they are willing to co-operate in an Examination Team (see 1.4) which will visit the candidate NSI. The Secretary shall send warning letters to those NAls and to those NSls which have not sent in their replies within six weeks of the date of despatch. If no reply is received by the end of the three months, it shall be assumed that the NAI in question has no objections and, if applicable, agrees with the choice of a mentor, and that the NSI is willing to join the Examination Team. 1.3.2 Objections shall be raised in a letter to the Secretary with a copy to the candidate. The Secretary shall ask the candidate whether it can meet each of the objections or prefers a discussion in the ICC. In the latter case, the Secretary shall circulate the relevant objections received to all NAls in a letter, asking whether the individual objections are supported by other members. The situation shall preferably be discussed at a meeting held in accordance with 001002-1, subclause 3.6 and to which the candidate is invited to send a representative. Either the NSSA is accepted if the individual objections find no support, or the candidate is required to change it in accordance with a recommendation from the ICC. 1.3.3 If it is not possible to hold the meeting within six months of the date of receipt of the request made in the reply by the candidate, the candidate may request that the matter be concluded in writing. In this case, it may prepare a written statement disputing the objections, which shall be circulated, together with the objections, to all NAls and NSls. The NAls shall state, within three months of the circulation, whether they support the objections. Each specific item of an objection shall be sustained only if supported by at least two further NAls. The voting period shall be terminated when all NAls have replied or three months after circulation, whichever is the shorter. 12

ac

IS ac 001002-3: 2000 IEC ac 001002�3 (1998)

1.4

Nomination of the Examination Team

1.4.1 As soon as the NSSA has been approved, the Chairman of the ICC shall submit for the 001002-1 , subclause 3.7.2, the approval of full members of this Committee, in accordance with names of three NSls to form the Examination Team from amongst those which have stated a willingness to participate . The Examination Team shall consist of one representative from each of the three NSls chosen by them from the list of team members (see 1.4.2).

ac

An NSf acting as a mentor for the candidate shall not serve on the Examination Team . Each member of the designated Examination Team may be assisted by not more than two support staff from their NSI. 1.4.2 The Secretariat shall maintain a list of Examination Team members. nominated by their NSI. This list shall include the following information: name of member; duty or position within the NSI; business address . 1.4.3 The candidate shall only be responsible for the transportation and living expenses of the three members of the Examination Team, whether this is an initial visit or. if necessary, a subsequent visit. The visits within the country of the candidate shall be planned so that they will be completed as expeditiously as possible . 1.4.4 The Examination Team shall elect one of its members as Chairman. The Secretary of the ICC shall, in consultation with all persons involved, make the arrangements for a visit of the Examination Team to the candidate. The visit shall take place. unless impractical, within three months of the approval of the NSSA.

1.5
1.5.1 a) b) c) d)

Examination procedure
The Examination Team during its visit to the candidate shall verity that the candidate meets the general requirements of 1.1.1 and 1.1.2; the Basic Rules and Rules of Procedure have been implemented in a correct way; the NSSA is a correct description of the actual situation; the candidate has sufficient experience with quality assessment of electronic components (see 1.5.2) and has arrangements for the preparation and maintenance of a list of approved manufacturers. distributors, specialist contractors and independent testing laboratories which it has assessed and intends to approve under the System.

1.5.2 Sufficient experience with quality assessment of electronic components is assumed to exist when the candidate a) has processed at least one request by a manufacturer for approval and

13

IS OC 001002-3: 2000 lEe OC 001002�3 ( 1G98)

b)

has processed at least two applications for approval of components. The procedures shall have been earned out In a manner Similar to these Rules of Procedure and with specifications defining the quality conformance tests required for Qualification Approval (QA) , Capability Approval (CA), or the Inspection requirements of the Customer Detail Specification (CDS) for Technology Approval (TA).

If this experience IS not available at the time of application, the candidate may request that one of the NSls acts as its mentor (see 1.31) The NAI of the candidate's country shall delegate, to the NSI accepting to act as mentor . the responsibility for the surveillance of all procedures for quality assessment necessary for the System In the candidate's country for an initial period until the candrdate has acqurred sufficient experience . DUring the initial period. the mentor shall supervise in the candIdate's country the operation of the candidate and countersign all approvals. certificates and reports as appropriate These approvals are consequently valid under the System . The candidate shall inform the ICC when it considers it is ready for the visit by the Examination Team 1.5.3 The candidate shall be responsible for arranging visits by the Examination Team to its laboratory and to any other Iaboratones to which it will have direct access in the framework of the System so that the Examination Team can decide if the candidate has the ability and capacity to carry out all the normal measurements that may be required . It may also be required to arrange visits to a callbratton laboratory used in the calibration chain. The candidate shall also arrange a Visit to one manufacturer's production line which has been subjected to the procedures of the System . Copies of the relevant component specification which shall be In one of the IEC official languages (see Article 20 of the Statutes of the IEC), shall be sent In advance to the member of the Examination Team. The specification shall define series of the tests specnied for the release of components under the System . The candidate may. if he considers It helpful, arrange visits to manufacturers in other technological areas covered by his application In addItion to that shown during the VISit. the Examination Team may discuss with the candidate any other part of Its declared technological area Dunng the visit to the manufacturer. the Examination Team shall have access to the documentation referred to In ISO 9000 standards and required in 32 which is relevant to the component production under reV18w. The earlier prOVision of thiS documentation shall be at the manufacturer's discretion This documentation may be in any language . the candidate being responsible for providing oral translation Into one of the offiCial languages of the IEC at the time of the visit.

1.6

Reporting and decision

1.6.1 DUring the VISIt. the Examination Team shall prepare a draft of its formal report. This draft shall contain all the conclusions of the Examination Team where these are either the joint opinions of the Exarmnation Team or those of one or two of Its members. The report shall Indicate whether a) b) the Examination Team would unanimously recommend the approval of the candidate: or it would recommend, subject to the correction of some minor deficiencies. the approval of the candidate . or there were important defidencies and the Examination Team could not recommend approval until these deficiencies had been corrected and a further visit by one or more members of the team would be necessary to deterTntne whether the corrective action was satisfactory: or

1.6.7 If the Examination Team unanimously recommends in its report the approval of the candidate, this recommendation shall be submitted to the full members of the ICC for voting by correspondence (see 001002-1, subclause 3.7.2 and 3.7.3). Approval shall not be withheld by any full member except for technically valid and documented reasons.

The decision of the ICC shall be circulated to the CMC for confirmation (see subclause 2.8.4b).

ac 001002-1 ,

1.6.8 If the candidate does not agree with the report of the Examination Team, it shall be allowed to present its case in writing to the ICC prior to this Committee considering the recommendation of the Examination Team. The delegates of full members, who are members of NSls, shall consider this matter during the first scheduled meeting of the ICC following the submission of the report from the Examination Team and the objections from the candidate, provided these have been submitted at least six weeks prior to this meeting. The ICC shall give a decision in writing within one month of the meeting. In cases where the next meeting of the ICC is scheduled for a date of six months or more after the submission of the report of the Examination Team and the objections of the candidate, the latter may request a meeting of the ICC to consider and decide on this matter. The Chairman of the ICC shall immediately arrange for this meeting to be held. If the ICC concurs with the recommendations of the Examination Team, and if the candidate still considers that its views were not properly taken account of or that the correct procedures were not followed by the ICC, the candidate may appeal against the decision of the latter to the CMC. During its first scheduled meeting, the CMC shall deal with the appeal, provided that the appeal has been submitted at least six weeks prior to the meeting. If the CMC agrees with the appeal, the ICC shall be instructed to reconsider the approval of the candidate. If the CMC does not agree with the appeal, the candidate shall implement the necessary corrections.

1.7

Changes in the NSSA

1.7.1 Changes in an NSSA, such as those on 1.2.2b), d) and e), which could affect the adequate supervision of approved manufacturers, distributors, specialist contractors and independent testing laboratories, shall be submitted to the Secretariat and shall be approved by the ICC before taking effect. The Secretariat shall circulate the proposed changes to the members of the ICC with a request that they state within six weeks of despatch from the Secretariat whether they have any objections.

The Secretariat shall send warning letters to those members which have not sent in their replies
within four weeks of the date of despatch. Objections to proposed changes shall be accompanied by valid reasons. If no objections and no requests to discuss the matter at a meeting to be held are received by the end of the six weeks, the relevant NSI shall be informed of this and the Secretary shall report this at the next meeting of the ICC. In all other cases, the matter shall be dealt with at the next meeting of the ICC. The decision of the ICC may be such that an examination visit is required, in which case the scope of the visit shall be defined and it shall be assigned to two NSls.

16

IS ac 001002-3: 2000 IEC ac 001002-3 ( 1998 )

1.7.2 The NSI shall within one month notify the Secretariat of changes to the NSSA other than those given in 1.7.1 The Secretariat shall circulate such notification to all members . 1.7.3 Each NSI is respons ible for deciding whether the action on changes should be subjected to the procedures of 1.7 .1 or 1.7.2. If no objections are received by the end of six weeks, the relevant NSI shall be informed of this and the Secretary will report this at the next meeting of the ICC. If objections are received , the matter shall be dealt with at the next meeting of the ICC. Pending the decision of the ICC, the change shall be considered as not having been approved and the relevant NSI shall be informed of this fact. 1.7.4 When one or more objections have been received, the NSI proposing NSSA may request that the matter be concluded in writ ing, if it is not possible to the ICC within six months of the receipt of the objection(s). In this case , it may statement disput ing the objection(s) , which shall be circulated together with the NAls and NSls , with a request to state whether they support the objections . the change to its hold a meeting of prepare a written objection(s) to all

Each specific item of an objection shall be sustained only if supported by at least two further NAls . The voting period shall be terminated when all NAls have replied or six weeks after circulation . whichever is the shorter. 1.7.5 Every three recapitulation of the procedures given in shall confirm that the years, the NSls approved under the System shall send to the Secretar iat a changes applied in their NSSA. The recapitulation shall be subjected to the 1.7.1. If no changes have been applied during the three year period. the NSI existing text is still valid.

1.8.1 1.8.1.1 a)

Maintenance, suspension and withdrawal of approval of an NSI Maintenance of approval
Every year, each NSI shall provide the following information for consideration by the ICC:

a written statement that there has been no change to the procedures in force , or an amendment to the NSSA if the changes are small , or a complete re-issue of the NSSA if the changes are of a significant nature: the number of approved manufacturers , distributors, specialist contractors and independent testing laboratories and an indication as requested in 1.2.5 of the frequency of surveillance visits ; a statement of the resources available with respect to those described in 1.2.7 for manpower and test facilities; list of the different families of components within the NSf's area of technological jurisdiction and which are under surveillance, identifying the associated generic specifications; the number of audit tests or other product verification activities performed either by the NSI or on its behalf; information on the annual internal audits conducted in accordance with 1.2, and a statement on verification of the corrective actions required ;
17

b)

IS QC 001002-3: 2000 lEe QC 001002-3 ( 1G9S )
g)

information, including the result, on any appeals against the decisions of the NSI or NCB which have needed resolution by the NAI or the ICC. This information shall be given in such a manner that it does not disclose any confidential information.

1.8.1.2 The ICC shall consider the information required by 1.8.1.1 at its next meeting and, if satisfied by the submission, shall so notify the NSI in writing within twenty-eight days. If the ICC is not satisfied, it may ask for further information to clarify any matters of doubt, either by an oral statement at the meeting or by further documentation. In the second case the final decision shall be made at the following meeting of the ICC. During this period, the approval of the NSI shall remain in force. 1.8.1.3 At intervals of not more than five years, the arrangements in the NSSA shall be reexamined by an Examination Team, chosen as prescribed in 1.7.1 (last paragraph) to assess the continued technical competence of the NSI to exercise its duties. 1.8.2 Suspension and withdrawal of approval

1.8.2.1 If evidence has been presented to, and accepted by, the ICC that components which do not conform to the requirements of the System and to the relevant specifications are being released and that the NSI, NCB and the NAI concerned have been informed and have failed to take any remedial action, the ICC shall immediately suspend the approval of the NSI. All NAls, NCBs and NSls shall be informed in writing by the Secretary of the ICC within twenty-eight days of the decision to suspend the approval of the NSI. 1.8.2.2 The ICC may require the NSI to submit evidence that it has corrected its deficiencies or may decide to convene an Examination Team to re-assesses the NSI. The final decision on the outcome shall be made at the next meeting of the ICC. If the decision is to lift the suspension, the NSI may resume its activities immediately and confirmation of the lifting of the suspens ion shall be given in writing by the Secretary of the ICC within twenty-eight days to all NAls, NCBs and NSls. If the decision is unfavourable or corrective actions have not been completed within six months, or any other period agreed by the ICC, the procedures of 1.8.2.3 shall be invoked. 1.8.2.3 Where the deficiencies are serious, the ICC may withdraw approval of the NSI . Formal notification of the withdrawal of the approval shall be given, in writing, to the NSI, by the Secretary of the ICC within twenty-eight days of the decision . The decision, however, shall be binding from the time that it was made by the ICC. All NAls. NCBs and NSls shall be informed by the Secretary of the ICC in writing within twenty-eight days of the withdrawal of the approval. Any SUbsequent request from the NSI to be re-admitted to the System shall be subject to the full procedures specified in clause 1 when new candidates apply for approval. 1.8.2.4 The voting on the decision for renewal or reinstatement of the approval of an NSI shall be on the same basis as that for the initial approval of an NSI. 1.8.2.5 An NSI has the right to appeal to the CMC against the decision made by the ICC. The decision of the ICC shall remain, pending the outcome of the appeal. Such an appeal shall be made within six months of the date of the ICC decision. 1.8.2.6 During the period of suspension, or in the case of withdrawal of approval, the NAI of the country involved may make arrangements, with the assistance of and subject to approval by the ICC, for other NSls to' carry out the surveillance and audit testing work in order to safeguard. to the maximum possible extent, the position of approved organizations.

2. Requirements for the approval of an organization
2.1 Introduction

The IECa bases its requirements for the approval of the organization of a manufacturer, distributor or specialist contractor (supplier approval) on those of the ISO 9000 family of standards. The requirements for the organization approval of independent testing laboratories are based on the requirements of ISOIIEC Guide 25. or equivalent regional or national standards such as the European Standard EN 45001.

2.2

Non-discriminatory access to the System

Any manufacturer or distributor of electronic components, or specialist contractor or independent testing laboratory shall be allowed non-discriminatory access to the System and specifically to the use of attestation of conformity granted under the supervision of a National Supervising Inspectorate (NSI), subject to compliance with the Rules of the System.

2.3 2.3.1

Organization approval of a manufacturer, distributor or specialist contractor Application for approval

Any manufacturer wishing to become an approved manufacturer under the System in order to seek approval of components produced by him, or, any distributor, being independent of any manufacturer's production department and wishing to become an approved distributor under the System in order to stock and distribute approved components, or, any specialist contractor wishing to become an approved specialist contractor under the System, shall a) apply to the National Certification Body (NCB), giving the information required (see NOTE below), undertake to allow access by the representatives of the NSI to all parts of the location relevant to the System. These representatives shall not disclose, without the manufacturer's, distributor's or specialist contractor's prior permission, any confidential information obtained in the course of their duties, and, nominate a Designated Management Representative (DMR).
A National certification Body (NCB) is the organization designated in the national rules that has full

b)

c)
NOTE

responsibility for certification underthe System. In the application, the manufacturer shall indicate the generic and, if relevant, sectional specification against which he intends to produce components, the location of the factory (factories), or parts thereof, for which approval is sought. A separate application shall be submitted for each location, whether the manufacturer wishes to be approved for design control, or not, and

19

IS QC 001002-3: 2000 IEC QC 001002-3 (1998) that he has prepared the required documentation as a basis for the appraisal by the NSI and has available the resources to meet the requirements of the System; the distributor shall indicate the type(s) of components he wishes to supply under the System, the names of the approved manufacturers who have authorized him to stock and distribute their components, the location of the establishment(s) , or parts thereof, for which approval is sought. A separate application shall be submitted for each location, and that he has prepared the required documentation as a basis for the appraisal by the NSI and has available the resources to meet the requirements of the System; the specialist contractor shall indicate the range of activity, technology, processes and/or technical services for which he seeks approval, the Process Assessment Schedule(s) (PASs) in the ac 200000 series against which he intends to provide processes and/or technical services , the location of the premises, or parts thereof, for which the approval is sought. A separate application shall be submitted for each location, and that he has prepared the required documentation as a basis for the appraisal by the N51 and has available the resources to meet the requirements of the System. 2.3.2 Quality system requirements

The relevant provisions of ISO 900X: 1994 shall be met. Implementation of this requirement means that ISO 9002: 1994 shall be applicable as far as relevant for the component(s) or the range(s) of activity, technology(ies), process(es) and/or technical service(s) concerned. An applicant claiming design/development capability shall meet the requirements of ISO 9001: 1994. In this subclause, the numbering follows that of ISO 9001: 1994. Where ISO 9001 clauses are not specifically invoked , the provisions of those clauses apply without modification. Where the ISO 9001 clauses are referenced, the additional requirements of the IECa are given.

4.1.2.3 Management representative
The Designated Management Representative(DMR), provides a formal contact point for the NSI to enable the resolution of issues related to quality. See annex A of this clause for additional IECa provisions related to the activities of the DMR.

4.2 4.2.1

Quality system General

The quality system shall be defined and documented by means of a Quality Manual and supporting documentation. For IECa product/process-related approvals, requirements also exist for a capability Manual, Process Manual or Technology Approval Declaration Document(TADD), (see ac 001002-3, clauses 4, 5 and 6 respectively). 20

IS QC 001002-3: 2000 IEC QC 001002-3 (1998)

Compliance with this clause of the Rules of Procedure shall be confirmed by the NSI periodically. The period between such confirmations shall not exceed three years. Within this period all requirements shall be verified by the normal periodic auditing process. The organization shall notify the NSI in advance of any changes to the location of its approved facilities, or part thereof. If there is reason to suppose that there have been any changes affecting the approval at the new location, the NSI may require revalidation of the approval prior to the release of products processed, tested or distributed at the new location.

4.3 4.3.1

Contract review General

The purchaser's (customer's) requirements, as reflected in the contract, shall refer to the relevant IECQ documents or Customer Detail Specifications where these exist , or may alternatively refer to appropriate regional or internationally recognized publications.

4.4 4.4.1

Design control General

Where applicable, requirements for design control shall be implemented in accordance with QC 001002-3, clauses 3, 4, 5 and 6.

4.4.8

Design validation

The requirements of the IECQ for Qualification Approval, Capability Approval, Process Approval and Technology Approval embrace the requirements of ISO 9001: 1994 for design validation.

4.6 4.6.1

Purchasing General

In order to ensure that purchased product(s) conform(s) to a specified requirement, the IECQ defines a mechanism to permit specialist contractors in the electronic components industry to be approved in their own right for specific services or 001002-3, clause procedures or the manufacture of piece parts and materials (see

ac

5).
Component distributors shall be authorized by one or more approved manufacturer(s) to stock. repack. release and distribute their approved components. A distributor approved under the System is permitted to purchase released components from another approved distributor and deliver them provided that a)

the latter has purchased the components directly from an approved
manufacturer, and both distributors are authorized by the approved manufacturer to deliver the components . 21

b)

IS QC 001002-3: 2000 IEC QC 001002-3 ( 1998)

4.6.2

Evaluation of subcontractors

In satisfying the requirements of ISO 9001/9002: 1994, subclause 4.6.2, use should be made of ac 001002-3, clause 5 as guidance on the assessment of subcontractors. Subcontractors should preferably be approved under the IECa in accordance with the requirements of the ac 001002-3, clause 5. See annex B of this clause for additional IECa provisions relating to subcontracting.

4;6.3

Purchasing data

Purchasing data may be prepared jointly with the subcontractor and shall be clearty defined technically (for example, in a Customer Detail Specification) in order to ensure the quality of purchased product (including services).

4.6.4

Verification of purchased product

4.6.4.1 Supplier verification at subcontractors premises
The IECa requires the supplier to verify the satisfactory maintenance of the quality control procedures performed by his subcontractor (see annex B of this clause).

4.7

Control of customer-supplied product

Customer (purchaser)-supplied product is material (for example, raw or partly processed materials, piece parts, software, testing or production equipment) owned by the customer (purchaser) and which is necessary to complete the product in accordance with the contract. The supplier shall accept responsibility for prevention from damage, identification, maintenance, handling, use and storage of the customer (purchaser)-supplied product.

4.8

Product identification and traceability

The supplier shall establish procedures and maintain records for identifying individual batches of product for a minimum period (from the date of product release) of two years, or a longer period as defined by contractual, statutory or legal requirements. These records shall include documentation and specifications covering materials, production and testing, test results and release data. Further technologically-specific requirements shall be given in the relevant generic specification or assessment schedule. Reference shall be made to appropriate marking requirements.

4.9

Process control

In-process control is a mandatory feature of Technology Approval, and an implicit requirement of the IECa in general.

4.10

Inspection and testing

4.10.4 Final inspection and testing
Final inspection and testing requirements shall be as defined in the relevant specification, as required by the appropriate IECQ generic specification (GS), P~ Assessment SChedule (PAS) or Technology Approval Schedule{TAS).

22

IS QC 001002-3: 2000 lEe QC 001002-3 ( 1SXN1)

The NSI is permitted to select specimens at random and to subject them to such tests as are relevant for audit testing. The specimens shall be taken from production lots which have passed quality conformance inspection. and shall be returned to the manufacturer after testing , together with a test report. The number of specimens selected by the NSI shall not exceed the quantity normally required for approval tests. If the NSI wishes to carry out destructive tests, these tests may, by agreement with the manufacturer, replace those normally carried out by the manufacturer.

4.10.5 Inspection and tut records
Acceptance criteria shall be as defined in the relevant specification. Where applicable, a regional or internationally recognized specification shall be used for parts per million (ppm) systems, Assessed Process Average, etc ..

4.11

Control of Inspection, measuring and tut equipment

Compliance with ISO 10012-1 is a mandatory requirement of the IECO . Guidance for the determination of the uncertainty of measurement in accordance with ISO 10012-1 is given in annex C of this clause.

4.12

Inspection and tut stlltua

Release of conforming products shall be in accordance with OC 001002-2, clause 2. Certificates of approval and attestation of conformity.

4.13

Control of non-conformlng product

4.13.2 Review and disposition of non-conformlng product
Repair is the making good of an approved component which has been damaged or has become defective after release. and is not permitted under the IECO (see 001002-3, clauses 3, 4,5 and 6).

ac

Rework is the rectification of processing errors prior to the release of the component by means not differing from those used in the current process or the rework processes to an agreed procedure as permitted by the relevant GS, PAS or TAS. Specimens found to be non-conforming (defective) during lot-by-Iot testing shall be withdrawn from the lot and not delivered. Lots rejected in lot-by-lot testing may be resubmitted in accordance with the relevant sampling procedures, for example IEC 410, and with the requirements prescribed in the relevant specification controlling the sampling procedure. No inspection lot, or part of it, shall be submitted more than twice in total to the lot-by-Iot testing unless specifically allowed by the relevant generic. sectional IJr blank detail specification . In circumstances in which a responsible specification authority finds it necessary to make such allowances, the condit ions governing further resubmission of rejected lots should be specified in detail in the relevant specification in such a manner that the reasons for allowing such further resubmissions are clear.

23

IS QC 001002-3: 2000 IEC QC 001002-3 (1998)

4.15

Handling, storage, packaging, preservation and delivery

4.15.1 General
Where relevant, particular requirements are given in GSs, PASs or TASs for the following: - anti-static precautions(see also European Standard EN 100015); - cleanliness; - health and safety aspects of chemicals and materials.

4.15.2 Handling
The requirements of ISO 9001/9002: 1994 are applied by IECQ not only to the finished product, but also to partly-processed materials.

4.15.3 Storage
See also 4.13.1 of ISO 9001/9002: 1994 in respect of control of non-conforming product. QC 001002-2, clause 2, Certificates of approval and attestation of conformity, and the relevant specifications prescribe procedures for the date coding of components andlor associated packaging. Procedures for ensuring the validity of release are contained in QC 001002-3, clauses 3, 4, 5 and 6. Shelf-life and revalidation requirements are detailed in the applicable specifications.

4.15.4 Packaging
For electronic components, sub-assemblies or assemblies, it is necessary to distinguish between integral packaging, which is the case or body of the component itself, intimate packaging, which is enveloping material which makes immediate contact with components, sub-assemblies or assemblies (sometimes referred to as "primary packaging"), and

- transit or storage packaging, which is protective packaging for delivery of product and transporting/storing items during manufacture (sometimes referred to as "secondary packaging"). Requirements for integral and intimate packaging are given in the relevant technical specification. For the protection of electrostatically sensitive devices, the requirements of generic specifications, or in European Standard EN 100015-1, shall apply.

4.15.5 Preservation
The relevant technical specifications may require the control of humidity and other environmental factors.

4.16

Control of quality records

The term "Quality Records" includes records related to IECQ approval activities as well as to activities covered by approvals against the requirements of ISO 9OOX: 1994.

24

IS ac 001002-3: 2000 IEC OC 001002�3 ( 1D9a ) Except as specified in ISO 900X: 1994, subclause 4.8, these records shall be maintained for a minimum of two years or, if applicable, a period not less than the periodic test frequency if this is longer than two years, and access shall be made available to the NSI upon request.

4.19

Servicing

Whilst servicing in the form of repair is not permitted by IECa (see ac 001002-3, 4 .13.2), the concept of "after sales service" is required by Process Approval and Technology Approval, that is to say, organizations approved under the provisions of ac 001002-3, clauses 5 and 6 are required to maintain close liaison with customers, to advise on usage applications and to analyze any problems experienced and to assist in the disposal of non-conforming items .

4.20

Statistical techniques

The use of statistical process control {SPC} is optional in most IECQ approvals. However, the use of in-process control techniques, such as SPC, is required for Technology Approval, QC 001002-3, clause 6. 2.3.3

Appraisal

2.3.3.1 The manufacturer, distributor or specialist contractor shall demonstrate to the NSI, in respect of all activities relevant to the System, that he meets the requirements of the System as given in ISO 900X: 1994 and amplified in 2.3.2. In performing the appraisal, account shall be taken of any comparable approvals granted by a recognised international, regional or national accreditation{certification) body . The manufacturer shall invite the NSI to see those parts of the manufacturing process which are not considered to be commercially confidential and are appropriate to the approval being sought. Such parts of the manufacturing process which are considered to be commercially confidential shall nevertheless be under the surveillance of the manufacturers DMR who shall satisfy the NSI of the adequacy of the quality control arrangements. A specialist contractor shall, additionally, demonstrate compliance with the requirements of clause 5 and with the relevant PAS . 2.3.3.2 When the NSI has determined that the manufacturer, distributor or specialist contractor has met the requ irements of 2.3.3.1, written notice of approval shall be provided to him by the NCB.

Technical competence

The relevant provisions of ISOIIEC Guide 25, or equivalent regional or national standard, such as European Standard EN 45001, shall be met. In this subclause, the numbering follows that of ISO/lEe Guide 25: 1990. Where ISOIIEC Guide 25 clauses are not specifically invoked, the provisions of those clauses apply without modification. Where the ISO/IEC Guide 25 clauses are referenced, the additional requirements of the IECQ are given.

See annex A of this clause for additional IECQ provisions related to the activities of the DMR, a position comparable to that of the 'Technical Manager' of the laboratory.

14

SUbcontracting of calibration or testing

Subcontracting shall be to an independent testing laboratory with the required technical scope approved under the IECO, except when: the required service is not available from any approved independent testing laboratory within the System; the approved independent testing laboratory demonstrates to the NSI that other approved independent testing laboratories known to be operating in the relevant area of technology are unable to undertake the specified testing. When invoking these provisions, the approved independent testing laboratory shall produce a document which describes the surveillance arrangements by which it can be ensured that the testing to be carried out shall comply with the specification. Where possible the nominated testing laboratory shall be approved to ISOIIEC Guide 25 by a nationally recognized accreditation body. The document shall define how the nominated testing laboratory ensures that its relevant staff possesses the necessary competence and its relevant facilities are completely adequate for the purpose of the subcontracted testing, proposes to operate the subcontracted testing, and ensures that it has an adequate system for the calibration of its relevant measurement and test equipment and can provided adequate traceability to national standards.

In establishing the degree of surveillance necessary, account shall be taken of any current approvals and/or registration held by the nominated testing laboratory. Before authorizing the subcontracted testing, the approved independent testing laboratory shall demonstrate to the NSI that the proposed surveillance arrangements comply with the specification.

2.4.3

Appraisal

2.4.3.1 The independent testing laboratory shall demonstrate to the NSI, in respect to all activities relevant to the System, that it meets the requirements of the System, it meets the requirements of ISOIIEC Guide 25, or equivalent regional or national standard, and that it is sufficiently free from external influences which would prevent it from acting in an impartial manner. In performing the appraisal, account shall be taken of any comparable approvals granted by a recognized international, regional or national accreditation (certification) body. 2.4.3.2 When the NSI has determined that the independent testing laboratory has met the requirements of 2.4 .3.1 , written notice of approval shall be provided to the laboratory by the NCB.

d)

Organizations subject to one surveillance visit per year which fail to comply with the Rules of the System and/or have product or process failures shall .revert to the normal minimum frequency of surveillance.

2.7

Withdrawal or suspension of organization approval

2.7.1 Except as described in 2.7.2, when some part of the requirements described above for the approval, or for the extension of the approval , of a manufacturer, or of a distributor, independent testing laboratory or specialist contractor is no longer observed, the approval or the extension of the approval shall be withdrawn by the organization which granted it. If an approval of an organization is withdrawn, any relevant extension of approval shall also be withdrawn. 2.7.2 If the causes which may justify the withdrawal of approval are temporary, and it is demonstrated that they may be remedied after a brief delay, the approval shall be suspended by the organization which granted it.

2.7.3 The approval may also be withdrawn at the request of the manufacturer, distributor, independent testing laboratory or specialist contractor.
NOTE Adequate notice should be given of any intention to withdraw the productor service provided.

2.7.4 The approval of a manufacturer or distributor may be withdrawn if the manufacturer or distributor knowingly or intentionally makes any incorrect references to the manufacturer approval or misleading use of manufacturer approval information. The approval shall be withdrawn if a manufacturer or distributor fails to take corrective action in this respect within one month of being requested to do so by the relevant NCB.

2.7.5 A manufacturer, distributor, independent testing laborator/ or specialist contractor shall have the right to appeal, in accordance with the national arrangements, against the withdrawal of the approval. 30

Annex C to clause 2 (normative)

IECQ policy on uncertainty of measurement and inset limits

C.1

Objective

Specifications for electronic components used in the IECO give the parametric limits that define the acceptability of the component. These limits do not take into account the uncertainty of measurement caused by test and measuring equipment inaccuracies, test methods, environmental conditions and, sometimes, operator participation. The purpose of this annex is to define mandatory IECO policy on the calculation of measurement uncertainty and insetting limits to ensure uniform implementation of the rules of IECO. The special case of outsetting limits is also covered.

C.2

Definitions

C.2.1 uncertainty of measurement a statement of the limits of the range within which the true value of the measurement is expected to lie in relation to the recorded result with a defined confidence level C.2.2 measuring equipment
all of the instruments which are necessary in order to carry out a measurement. The definition makes it clear that items such as cables, connectors, handlers, handler cards or other fixtures used in conjunction with a measurement indicating instrument are subject to the requirements of this policy

C.2.3 inset limits
tightened limits resulting from an allowance applied to the specified limits of a parameter to take into account all influence quantities on the indication of a measuring instrument so as to ensure that out of limit devices are not accepted due to measurement errors

C.2.4 outset limits
relaxed limits resulting from an allowance applied to the specified limits of a parameter to take into account all influence quantities on the indication of a measuring instrument so as to ensure that in limit devices are not rejected due to measurement errors

C.3

Calculation of measurement uncertainty

The assessment of uncertainty of measurement of a performance requirement can be broken down into three stages : 1) 2) 3) identification of possible error contributions; quantifying the size of each listed contribution; calculating the total uncertainty of measurement.

37

IS ac 001002-3: 2000 IEC QC 001002-3 (1998)

C.4

Policy

C.4.1 A measurement uncertainty value shall be calculated for each performance requirement which is related to Qualification Approval, Capability Approval, Technology Approval, Process Approval, screening, lot-by-Iot and periodic tests as defined by the specifications of the IECQ . C.4.2 Each measurement uncertainty value shall be used to apply an inset, of at least this value, to the relevant specification limits as defined in C.4.1. C.4.3

This inset shall be applied in accordance with C.5.2 for manufacturers and C.5.3 for NSls.

C.4.4 Test reports and test records, compiled to show compliance with Qualification Approval, Capability" Approval, screening, lot-by-lot and periodic tests as defined by the applicable specifications, shall list the uncertainty value for each performance requirement.

C.S

Calculation of inset and outset Limits

C.5.1 The fundamental principle is that the limits should be inset from the specified values by the corresponding uncertainty of measurement. This increases the probability that measurement results which fall within the tightened limits, including marginal values, are genuinely within specification limits such that only truly conforming devices are accepted.

The exception to insetting limits occurs when NSls conduct product audit tests. In this situation, to ensure that, as far as possible, uncertainty of measurement does not cause good products to fail, NSls outset the limits. This increases the possibility that measurement results that fall outside the relaxed limits, including marginal values, are genuinely outside specification limits such that only truly non-conforming devices are rejected.
C.5.2 For a component manufacturer the upper specified value of a parameter being 'x', the lower specified value of the parameter being 'y' and the uncertainty of measurement being 'a', the "inset limits" for the parameter are (x-a) and (y+a). C.5.3 For an NSI the upper specified value of a parameter being 'x', the lower specified value of the parameter being 'y' and the uncertainty of measurement being 'b', the "outset limits" for the parameter are (x+b) and (y-b).

The smaller the uncertainty of measurement, the lower the values of 'a' and 'b' become and the closer the manufacturer's and NSf's inset/outset limits approach the specification limits.

C.6

Examples

Setting "inset limits" and "outset limits�
C.6.1 Example 1: Resistor Measurement

3. Qualification Approval of electronic components
3.0 Introduction

The Qualification Approval procedure is applicable to any electronic component, or range of components (for example, a range of resistors differing only in resistance values, tolerances and/or power ratings) when the appropriate specifications are notified in QG 001004, Specifications List, for use within the IEGQ System.

3.1
3.1.1

Procedure for Qualification Approval (QA)
Eligibility for QA

3.1.1.1 QA may be granted only to a manufacturer who has been granted manufacturer's approval in accordance with the requirements of clause 2 including , as appropriate, those of ISO 9001 or ISO 9002 and, additionally, the requirements of this clause. These approvals may be carried out in parallel , although QA shall not be granted in advance of manufacturer's approval. 3.1.1.2 A component is eligible for QA in accordance with the System if the manufacturing process , commencing not later than that manufacturing operation which is called the "primary stage" (see QG 001002-2, clause 1 and lEG Guide 102, subclause 4.2 b� is carried out by one or more manufacturers approved in accordance with the requirements of clause 2 and under the direct supervision of the relevant Designated Management Representative (DMR) or local DMR. The rules for the extension of manufacturer's approval given in clause 2 apply. 3.1.2

Use of specialist contractors and subcontracting

3.1.2.1 The primary stage and/or subsequent stages may be carried out by specialist contractors (see clause 2 ) or, under certain conditions, subcontracted (see 3.1.2.3 and 3.1.3 ). 3.1.2.2 The generic or sectional specification may

either forbid this subcontracting on technical grounds, or where it is considered necessary, include any special requirements, for example for specified successive stages to be performed by the same manufacturer, or permit the SUbcontracting unreservedly. Such restrictions shall not apply to arrangements made concerning specialist contractors. 3.1.2.3 When subcontracting is permitted by the generic or sectional specification, this may be undertaken provided that the DMR is able to demonstrate to the National Supervising Inspectorate (NSI) that the process(es) concerned is (are) a) performed in a manner which satisfies the appropriate requirements of the relevant Process Assessment Schedule (PAS), where such exists, or carried out satisfactorily.

details of the division of the manufacturing stages between the approved manufacturer and his company's factory located in a non-IECa member country, and details of the arrangements agreed with the NSI involved for the certification of the quality of the components taking into account the transfers carried out in the course of manufacture together with details of the means whereby changes to the agreed arrangements are communicated to the responsible NSI. The NSI of the manufacturer seeking QA shall ensure that the DMR of the approved manufacturer has effective responsibility for quality control procedures performed under the supervision of the local DMR on the production in a non-IECa member country, and ensure that the manufacturer possesses sufficient engineering capability and/or technical expertise to develop, maintain and control the manufacturing processes that he wishes to subcontract. or that the stages of manufacture concerned are adequately covered by the specialist contractors' existing approvals under the System.

3.1.3.5 When the manufacturer is ready to commence QA testing he shall give notice to the NSI of his intention to start tests and establish together with the NSI a test plan and a time schedule for the execution of the approval tests. 3.1.3.6 The' NSf shall check the appli~on for completeness of all required information and existence of the relevant detail specification. If any details are missing, further information shall be requested from the applicant. If the information is complete, the NSI shall send the manufacturer a
confirmation of application.

3.1.4

QA testing

QA testing may be carried out on a) a fixed sample as defined in the generic or sectional specification. In this case the sample shall be drawn from current production. or 43

IS QC 001002-3: 2000 lEe QC 001002-3 (1998) b) a specified number of inspection lots (with a minimum of three) taken in as short as possible a period of time, as well as the performance of the periodic tests on a sample taken from at least one of these lots , or sample quantities drawn from one lot only, sufficient to give acceptance on zero rejects. If the lot size is less than the resulting sample size, 100% testing shall be carried out. Normal sampling requirements for destructive tests shall apply. For inspection lots less than 25, the sample for destructive tests may comprise of components taken from several inspection lots whose total quantity exceeds 25. This procedure is only permitted when subsequent inspection lot sizes are predicted not to exceed 280 components (see NOTE), and the additional requirements given below shall be applied to lot sentencing following the granting of QA in this manner. All released components shall be individually subjected to the non-destructive tests specified in the detail specification, until satisfactory results have been achieved on cumulative quantities equal to the sample sizes required to give acceptance on three rejects for the lot-by-lot tests, or one reject for the periodic tests. Lot sizes may not subsequently be increased above those declared until satisfactory results have been achieved for all tests, on at least a sufficient quantity of components to meet the requirements given in this subclause (3.1.4) for the increased lot size .
NOTE When structural similarity is invoked for a subgroup, the relevant inspection lot size is the total of all types considered similar for that subgroup.

c)

When components cover a range of values or characteristics, the sample shall contain specimens which are representative of the range for which QA is being sought. The sample shall also be representative of the manufacturing process. The tests shall be carried out by either the approved manufacturer, an approved independent testing laboratory, an NSI or, exceptionally, in accordance with the requirements specified in 3.1.2.7.

The results of the tests shall be recorded in a QA Report prepared by the manufacturer in
accordance with annex B to this clause and authenticated by the DMR and verified by the agreement (countersignature) of the N51 that the QA Report meets the requirements of the specification. A copy of this report shall be submitted to the NCB as a recommendation. Any other reproduction and release of this report is the sale prerogative of the manufacturer

3.1.5

Granting of QA

The NCB shall validate the recommendation and grant the QA, when the requirements of 3.1.4 have been met.

3.1.6

QA certificate

When QA has been granted, a certificate shall be issued to the manufacturer in accordance with ac 001002-2, clause 2. The component or range of components shall be listed in QC 001005, Register of Firms , Products, and Services approved under the IECa System, including ISO 9000. The above information shall be communicated to any customer on request.

Subject to the requirements above, there is no limit to the duration of the validity of the QA. Procedure in the event of failure in a periodic test

3.1.8.1 When a sample fails to satisfy the requirements of a periodic test the DMR (or, where applicable, the local DMR) shall immediately suspend further releases under the Mark, or Certificate, of Conformity of the component in question, initiate an investigation to determine the reasons for failure, and report the situation to the NSI. 3.1.8.2 The DMR (or, where applicable, the local DMR) shall maintain this suspension until the investigation has been concluded and the NSI has been informed of the results. The DMR (or, where applicable, the local DMR) shall then proceed according to the appropriate conditions in 3.1.8.3, 3.1.8.4 or 3.1.8.5. 3.1.8.3 a) b) If the failure is concluded to have been due solely to an error in test procedure,

release under the Mark, or Certificate of Conformity shall be resumed immediately, and the correct test procedure shall be applied to a sample drawn from the first available inspection lot. If the sample fails the corrected test, action shall be taken as in 3.1.8.1.
If the failure is concluded to be due to an identified manufacturing fault which can

3.1.8.4

immediately be corrected,

a)

release under the Mark, or Certificate, of Conformity of corrected lots shall be resumed immediately, the test shall be repeated on the first available corrected lot, and

b) c)

if the result of the repeated test is unsatisfactory, the procedure defined in 3.1.8.5 or 3.1.8.6 shall be applied as appropriate.

3.1.8.5 If the failure is concluded to be due to an identified manufacturing fault which cannot be corrected immediately, but defective components ca~ be detected and rejected by an appropriate eliminating test acceptable to the DMR (or, where applicable, the local DMR),

a)

b)

3.1.8.6 If the failure is concluded to be due to an identified manufacturing fault which cannot be corrected immediately and defective components cannot be removed by the application of an eliminating test, the NSI shall recommend to the NCB (see 3.1.12) that they suspend QA and withdraw the right to use the Mark, or Certificate, of Conformity for the component in question . QA and the right to use the Mark, or Certificate, of Conformity shall be reinstated when the manufacturer can demonstrate , by the successful submission of a sample from a production lot to the periodic test, that the manufacturing fault has been eliminated. 3.1.8.7 If the failure cannot be attributed with certainty to a specific error in test procedure or to an identified manufacturing fault, samples from subsequent lots shall then be subjected to all tests in the subgroup of the periodic test in which the failure occurred, on a lot-by-Iot basis, and these lots may be released if these samples pass the test successfully. The sample size shall be that designated for the subgroup. Except where otherwise specified in the generic specification, normal periodic testing shall be resumed when two successive lots have successfully passed the tests in the subgroup in question, or as otherwise specified in the generic specification. 3.1.8.8 If the requirements of 3.1.8.4, or 3.1.8.5 or 3.1.8.6 are not fulfilled within a reasonable period of time, QA shall be re-examined and may be withdrawn. 3.1.8.9 If the duration of the periodic test in question exceeds three months and if special conditions would be appropriate to the particular type of component and the nature or extent of the failure, the relevant specification shall prescribe any special procedure to be followed. 3.1.9
Modifications likely to affect QA

3.2
3.2.1

Release for delivery and validity of release
General

~uality conformance inspection and periodic testing requirements for components are given, either directly or by reference, in published detail specifications.

3.2.2

Validity of release

A release for delivery is valid for five years unless a shorter period is specified in the deta il specification. The relevant specification shall prescribe the tests which shall be repeated in order to revalidate the release.

3.2.3 3.2.3.1

Quality conformance inspection General

Quality conformance is established after carrying out tests demonstrating that the inspection lots (see 3.3) have achieved the quality prescribed in the specification. The manufacturer shall carry out these tests, or arrange to have them carried out in a laboratory approved under the System . The detail specification shall prescribe those tests which have to be performed. The acceptability of the lot is determined by the requirements of the specification. When quality conformance inspection is performed according to 3.1.3.1d} in a factory located in a non-/ECQ member country, samples of each inspected lot manufactured in that factory shall, for a period of time determined by the NSI and agreed by the Inspectorate Co-ordination Committee (ICC) , be sent to the manufacturer in the IECa member country. These samples shall be used for audit testing by the NSI or by the manufacturer on behalf of the NSI. and the results of these audit tests compared with the results of the quality conformance inspection to validate the sentencing of each lot.

3.2.3.2

Lot-by-Iot tests

Lot-bY-lot tests are carried out on each inspection lot. These tests may be divided into two groups: Group A , covering visual and dimensional inspection of the components and the principal characteristics of the components (initial measurements); Group B, covering additional important characteristics. Each group may Le divided into two or more subgroups.

47

IS QC 001002-3: 2000 IEC QC 001002-3 (1998)

3.2.3.3

Periodic tests

Periodic tests are carried out at fixed intervals on samples taken from lots which have already satisfied the lot-by-lot tests. These periodic tests are generally brought toget~er and ~esignated Group C tests. These can be divided into subgroups , for example, on the basis of the Interval at which the samples are taken. Sometimes a Group D may be included containing additional tests required for the maintenance of

CA.
3.2.3.4 Destructive tests

Specimens which have been subjected to destructive tests shall not be included in lots to be delivered. Specimens subjected to non-destructive tests may be included in lots to be delivered provided they satisfy the specified tests.

3.2.3.5

Use of in-process testing

In-process testing may be substituted for the relevant test(s) of the quality conformance testing provided that the manufacturer demonstrates that the in-process testing is such that the corresponding requirements of the specification would have been met at the final stage of inspection.

3.2.3.6

Test severity

A manufacturer may carry out any test at a greater severity than that specified, but the component after testing shall satisfy the limits prescribed in the specification.

3.2.3.7

Alternative test methods

The test and measurement methods given in the relevant specification are intended to unify test and measurement procedures . They are not necessarily the only methods which can be used except when specifically designated as referee or reference methods. The approved manufacturer shall demonstrate to the NSI that any alternative methods he uses will give results equivalent to those obtained by the specified method.

3.2.3.8

Measurement uncertainty

The limits prescribed in specifications are true values. When carrying out the specified tests the approved manufacturer shall employ sufficient inset from the specified limits to cover the uncertainty of his measurement (see annex C of clause 2).

3.2.4

Non-conforming components in lot-by-Iot tests

S~mens found non-conforming during lot-by-tot testing shall be withdrawn from the lot and not dehve~ed. ~ots rejected in lot-by-Iot tests may be resubmitted in accordance with the requirements prescnbed In the relevant specification .

3.2.5

Non-conformances in periodic tests

The DMR shall .~eep records of non-conformances observed in samples subjected to periodic tests where the repetition of such non-conformances may lead to the suspension or withdrawal of QA (see 3.1.10 and 3.1.12).

48

IS QC 001002�3: 2000 IEC QC 001002�3 (1998)

3.2.6

Release or rejection of lots

Except wh~n otherwise prescribed in the relevant specification, the lots shall be released or rejected on the basis of the lot-by-lot tests (see 3.2.3.2). The failure of the sample submitted to one of the periodic tests shall entail the rejection of the lot from which the sample came unless release has already taken place due to the length of the test.

3.2.7

Identification of released lots

Lots released by manufacturers or distributors shall be unambiguously identified by a Mark, or Certificate, of Conformity, the affixing, or issue, of which is under the surveillance of the NSI. This Mark, or Certificate, means that the components have been released in accordance with the 001002-2, clause 2, Certificates of approval requirements of the relevant detail specification (see and attestation of conformity).

ac

Only components approved against a detail specification registered within the System may receive the Mark, or Certificate, of Conformity. Authorization to affix, or to issue, the Mark, or Certificate, of Conformity is suspended or withdrawn if there is persistent non-conformity with the specification (see 3.1.10 and 3.1 .12) or if the provisions of this clause 3 are not observed.

3.2.9

Customer returns and appropriate corrective action

An approved component retumed for non-technical reasons, provided that the package is unopened and undamaged and its original labelling is intact, may be returned to the approved manufacturer's bonded store for release. Approved manufacturers shall notify the NSI every six months of non-conformities on components released under the System. Notification shall be given in writing and may be presented during a surveillance/audit visit, or otherwise as agreed with the NSI.

3.3.1

Inspection lots
Fonnation of inspection lots

An inspection lot may be formed by the aggregation of several production lots provided that
a)

the production lots are manufactured under essentially the same conditions (materials, processes, machines, personnel, etc.), and, quality control and inspection dUring manufacture is performed to the extent necessary, in accordance with directives established by the appropriate departments of the manufacturer in consultation with the DMR, and,

b)

c)

the results of this inspection indicate for each production lot that the quality of materials and processing is maintained within the limits necessary for the production of components satisfying the requirements of the specification, and, the period over which production lots may be aggregated into one inspection lot shoUld normally not exceed one week, and shall not exceed one month unless permitted by the relevant specification. 50

d)

IS QC 001002�3: 2000 lEe QC 001002�3 (1998)

The programme for the aggregation of production lots into inspection lots shall be determined by the DMR and shall be submitted for approval to theNSI.

3.3.2

Structurally similar components

Structurally similar components are components produced by the same manufacturer with essentially the same design. materials, processes and methods. They are such that the results of a given test carried out on one of these components can be recognised as being valid for the others of the group . They are separately identifiable. The relevant specification shall give the requirements for grouping structurally similar components for the purpose of testing for QA and quality conformance inspection.

Detail specifications for components

The detail specifications shall comply with the requirements of the blank detail specifications .

Annex B to clause 3
(normative)

Qualification Approval Report
8.1 General

The overall format of an approval report is flexible and the specific style can be chosen to suit individual preferences but, as a minimum, the report shall contain the following information:

8.2

Preface

The approval report shall be prefaced as follows: approval report title, reference number and date; detail specification , issue number and associated product references; name, address and approval number of manufacturer; name, address and status of independent testing laboratory (if appropriate); name and address of the responsible NSI; a dated declaration signed by the DMR as follows : "I certify that the requirements of the System have been met and that all samples tested were either 1) 2) taken from, and are representative of, current production ; or manufactured using currentlintended production methods and materials." NSI signature and date.

8.3

Index, page identification and detail specification

The approval report shall contain an index summarizing its contents and identifying the respective page numbers for major sections. All approval report pages shall be numbered. It is recommended that a copy of the applicable detail specification be included as an annex to the approval report.

8.4 Test plan and summary of results
Details of all samples shall be given, including batch identity and date code. The approval report shall contain a summary of the test plan agreed with the NSI and attributes data for the respective test samples, preferably in tabular format. Where structural similarity is being claimed, full details shall be given, inclUding reference(s) to previously agreed approval reports (when applicable).

54

IS QC 001002-3: 2000 IEC QC 001002-3 ( 1_)

8.5 Test equipment and results
The test and measurement equipment used during the Qualification Approval exercise shall be uniquely identified and its calibration status shown. The measurement uncertainty associated with each test shall be stated and taken into account when determining pass/fail criteria. For every test method, the report shall state the methocl used by reference to the appropriate standard or detail specification. Where a non-standard method is used, fUll details shall be given. All test conditions shall be described. If full details are given in the applicable detail specification. reference to the particular subgroup will suffice. The test results shall be specified accurately, clearly and completely. The results of each test sequence/subgroup shall be dated and identified as to the individual who performed the test. Where there is a large amount of test data, it is recommended that a statistical form of presentation is used.

8.6 Failure identification and analysis
Any failures which occur during Qualification Approval testing shall be identified and the failure cause analyzed. The results of this analysis shall be included in the test report. Where corrective action is indicated, details shall be given .
